skill.name: ac-nexus
skill.description: AI agent guidance for AC-Nexus, a Python smart air conditioner control library for Broadlink RM and Xiaomi MIoT IR devices.
skill.summary: Control Broadlink and Xiaomi MIoT air conditioners with agent-guided setup, weather checks, schedules, and logs.
skill.author: oywq00008-cell

security_audit.summary: Most external-command findings are false positives from Markdown code spans and fenced examples, not executable Ruby backticks. Confirmed risks include hidden durable configuration, API key and device-token handling, persistent physical-device automation, and privacy-sensitive IoT device inventory collection.

remediation.issue: Hidden durable configuration stores sensitive device data and API keys.
remediation.suggestion: Document exact file paths, restrict permissions, support secret redaction, and provide a clear cleanup command for ~/.ac_controller.

remediation.issue: Schedules and storm shutdown behavior can persist after the agent task ends.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation before enabling persistent automation and provide a single disable command in every automation workflow.

remediation.issue: Xiaomi QR login and device token handling expose sensitive account and local device credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before login, avoid logging sessions or tokens, and recommend secure storage with least required retention.

remediation.issue: Documentation includes a realistic token-shaped value in a device example.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the token with an obvious placeholder such as YOUR_DEVICE_TOKEN and state that real tokens must never be shared.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent Physical Device Automation
semantic_findings.description: The skill directs agents to create durable schedules and a background scheduler that can keep turning physical air conditioners on or off after the task ends. The file warns about confirmation, but the persistent physical automation remains a safety and consent risk.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The referenced lines explicitly describe durable state, a scheduler daemon, persistent schedule changes, and storm auto-shutdown behavior.

semantic_findings.title: Cloud Login Stores Local Device Tokens
semantic_findings.description: The Xiaomi setup flow obtains a QR login session, lists account devices, copies device identifiers and tokens, then saves them to local configuration. This is expected for MIoT control but creates sensitive account and device-token handling risk.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code sample shows QR login, device enumeration, token extraction, and persistent config saving in one flow.

semantic_findings.title: Credential-Like Device Token in Example
semantic_findings.description: A MIoT example passes a 32-character token-like value directly to a Device constructor. Even if illustrative, publishing concrete token-shaped values can normalize pasting long-lived device tokens into prompts or logs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The line contains a private LAN IP and a realistic long hex token in a device-control example, but it may be a placeholder rather than a live secret.

content.user_title: Control Air Conditioners with AI Agents
content.value_statement: Managing mixed Broadlink and Xiaomi IR air conditioners from an agent can be hard. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through setup, local control, weather checks, schedules, and logs.
actual_capabilities: Guides installation and initialization of the AC-Nexus Python library.
Controls Broadlink RM and Xiaomi MIoT IR air conditioner devices.
Adds Xiaomi IR controllers through QR login, device listing, and MIoT spec matching.
Fetches weather and storm data for temperature decisions and shutdown workflows.
Manages schedules, auto-adjust settings, custom IR codes, and Markdown logs.
limitations: Requires compatible Broadlink or Xiaomi MIoT hardware on the local network.
Requires Python dependencies and external weather or Xiaomi services for some workflows.
Stores device configuration, API keys, and schedules in a hidden local config directory.
Persistent schedules and shutdown automation need explicit user approval before changes.

use_cases.title: Set Up Home AC Control
use_cases.description: Configure a Broadlink or Xiaomi IR controller so an agent can turn air conditioners on or off by room.

use_cases.title: Build Agent Workflows
use_cases.description: Connect Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to AC-Nexus routines for device selection, state checks, and safe command routing.

use_cases.title: Automate Weather Responses
use_cases.description: Use weather, temperature, and storm signals to adjust cooling or shut down devices with confirmation.

prompt_templates.title: Check Current Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Use AC-Nexus to review my configured air conditioner devices. Tell me what information you need before sending any control command.

prompt_templates.title: Control One Room
prompt_templates.prompt: Use AC-Nexus to turn on the air conditioner in the named room at 25 degrees cooling mode. Ask before changing saved schedules.

prompt_templates.title: Add Xiaomi Controller
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through adding a Xiaomi MIoT IR controller with QR login. Explain where tokens and device details will be stored.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Weather Automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a safe AC-Nexus workflow that uses weather and storm data. Include confirmation points before persistent automation is enabled.

output_examples.input: Check which air conditioner device is active.
output_examples.output: The active device is the configured living room controller. It is linked to the Broadlink provider and can receive IR commands.
The workflow asks you to scan the Xiaomi login QR code, lists eligible IR controllers, then saves the selected device for local control.

output_examples.input: Use storm information to protect the AC units.
output_examples.output: The workflow checks active storm distance and wind tier, then asks before pausing schedules or shutting down all configured devices.

best_practices: Confirm with the user before changing schedules, auto-adjust rules, device names, or storm shutdown behavior.
Use meaningful room names so agents can map natural language requests to the correct device.
Protect the hidden config directory because it may contain API keys, device tokens, and automation rules.
anti_patterns: Do not enable persistent schedules or auto-shutdown without explicit user approval.
Do not paste real device tokens, cloud sessions, or API keys into prompts or logs.
Do not assume example IP addresses or device models match the user environment.

faq.question: What devices does this skill support?
faq.answer: It targets Broadlink RM IR blasters and Xiaomi MIoT-compatible IR remote controllers used for air conditioner control.

faq.question: Does it require a desktop GUI?
faq.answer: No. The skill describes Python library workflows that agents can run without a graphical interface.

faq.question: Where is configuration stored?
faq.answer: The documentation says AC-Nexus stores configuration under a hidden .ac_controller directory in the user home folder.

faq.question: Can it use weather data?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents Baidu and QWeather weather sources plus storm checks from NMC and NHC data.

faq.question: Can it control more than one brand?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented provider model separates Broadlink and Xiaomi devices and routes commands by device type.

faq.question: What needs extra care?
faq.answer: Persistent schedules, API keys, Xiaomi device tokens, and physical device commands require careful confirmation and storage controls.
